subject: Clarify: evidence handover & subprocessor cooperation for privacy alert
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: security@finserv.com, dpo@finserv.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Clarify: evidence handover & subprocessor cooperation for privacy alert

Hi Alice / FinServ security team,

Thanks for flagging the alert this morning. Before we proceed with any data transfer, Legal asked me to clarify a few operational details so the DPA obligations and our incident-notification commitments align: 

1) Scope: can you confirm exactly which environment(s) and customer IDs are in scope (production vs staging, tenant IDs)? We want to avoid overbroad exports.

2) Timeline expectations: the DPA references "prompt" notification and cooperation; FinServ has previously asked for evidence within 48 hours. Our SOC2 evidence pipeline usually requires 72 hours to collect and redact logs across subprocessors. Are you able to accept a 72-hour evidence window for raw logs with an interim summary within 24 hours?

3) Subprocessor involvement: you requested access to subprocessor logs — we can provide redacted extracts and attestations. For full forensic exports that include subprocessor data, we need a written request and scoping so we can route to the subprocessor (some are third-party agents in EU). Any regulatory requirement driving a direct subprocessor handover?

4) Cross-border transfer: if the scope includes EU-resident data, we need to ensure SCCs / lawful transfer mechanisms are acknowledged and a controller-to-controller data flow is documented.

I'm attaching a short checklist (incident_evidence_checklist.xlsx) and a current data map (redwood-data-map.pdf) to speed technical triage. 

Proposed next steps: you confirm scope and minimum fields required, we produce an interim summary within 24 hours and start evidence collection with expected delivery T+72 hours. If you need full raw logs faster, we can escalate but may need a procurement/exception signoff.

Appreciate a quick confirmation so we can align our incident playbook with your timeline.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
jonas@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0199

Attachments: incident_evidence_checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet), redwood-data-map.pdf (report)

From: Alice Martin <dpo@finserv.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarify: evidence handover & subprocessor cooperation for privacy alert

Jonas — thanks, that helps. Quick answers below: 

- Scope: production tenant IDs FS-9812 and FS-9813 only. No staging.
- Timeline: our SLA language and internal regulators expect substantive evidence within 48 hours for incidents with potential customer personal data impact. An interim summary in 24 hours is fine.
- Subprocessors: we will require either (a) redacted extracts plus an attestation from the subprocessor, or (b) a controlled export if we can demonstrate regulator demand. Please advise which subprocessors hold logs for the two tenant IDs.
- EU transfer: some end-users are EU residents; we will need SCCs and a record of transfer safeguards.

We can be pragmatic: please send the 24-hour interim summary ASAP. If Redwood can commit to T+48 for key forensic items (auth logs, access traces for the tenant IDs), that would meet our regulatory ask. If not, please surface what blocks you from 48 hours (e.g., subprocessor coordination, legal redaction).

Cc'ing our security contact alice.security@finserv.com for technical follow-up.

Thanks,
Alice Martin
DPO, FinServ Solutions
alice.martin@finserv.com
+44 20 7946 0123

> On Dec 1, 2026, at 09:12, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com> wrote:
> 
> > Thanks for flagging the alert this morning...

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: alice.martin@finserv.com, security@finserv.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 10:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarify: evidence handover & subprocessor cooperation for privacy alert

Alice — appreciate the clarity. Below is our operational plan and what we can commit to without procurement/legal exceptions. 

Operational plan (proposed):
- T+24h (by 2026-12-02 09:12 PST): interim summary sent to FinServ (scope, systems affected, high-level indicator of PII types, containment steps).
- T+48h (by 2026-12-03 09:12 PST): prioritized forensic extracts for FS-9812/FS-9813: authentication events (last 30 days), IP traces, and access-control changes. These will be redacted for unrelated tenant data. Note: if the required extracts need coordination from an EU subprocessor (X-CacheLabs), delivery may extend to T+72h.
- T+72h (by 2026-12-04 09:12 PST): comprehensive artifact bundle, including aggregated KV cache traces, encryption key rotation events (KMS audit logs), and manifest of subprocessor attestation letters.

Constraints and asks from our side:
- Subprocessor list (we will share a minimal list) — if FinServ requires raw logs directly from a subprocessor, we need a written scoping request and proof of regulatory compulsion.
- Redaction standard: we will remove other customers' identifiers and apply a one-way hash to any PII not in scope. If you require plaintext PII for legal investigation, we'll need legal signoff and an NDA addendum.
- Cross-border transfers: if FinServ needs transfers from EU processors to FinServ legal entities, we will annotate each artifact with a transfer justification and rely on SCCs already in place. Please confirm whether FinServ will accept SCC+technical safeguards.

I have attached the checklist and data map again and added a proposed manifest format (sheet 2 of the checklist) for the artifacts. If this plan works, I'll have our security ops start preparing the interim summary immediately. 

Jonas

> Attachments: incident_evidence_checklist.xlsx, redwood-data-map.pdf

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 03 Dec 2026 15:30:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Clarify: evidence handover & subprocessor cooperation for privacy alert

Jonas — thanks for drafting the plan. Two operational notes from Legal/Compliance: 

1) Add a short SLA addendum: "Evidence delivery is best-effort within 48 hours for prioritized artifacts; full forensic bundles within 72 hours subject to subprocessor coordination and lawful transfer requirements." That helps manage customer expectations and avoids a hard 48-hour promise where subprocessors are involved.

2) For any artifact containing EU-resident data, include a transfer manifest that lists the legal basis (SCCs) and the minimal fields being transferred. We should also include a one-paragraph attestation template that the subprocessor can sign. I'll draft the attestation and send it to Marissa for ops review.

I'll Bcc Legal to ensure we have a record; Marissa, please confirm ops can meet the T+24 interim summary and the prioritized T+48 deliverable subject to the noted constraints.

—Laura Bennett
VP Legal, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com
